**Most likely: retinal neuron, probably an inner-nuclear-layer interneuron; subtype ambiguous.**

## Evidence
- **lhx4** — strongest localizing marker: expressed in nervous system, retina-associated adenohypophyseal/visual contexts, and specifically reported in zebrafish retinal ONL and INL; INL signal supports retinal interneuron identity but not a single subtype [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060728-1), [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-210123-21).
- **syt5b** — nervous-system expressed synaptic vesicle regulator; GO implicates calcium-dependent synaptic vesicle fusion, supporting a differentiated neuronal/synaptic state [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050522-134), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0099502).
- **gng13b** — expressed in retina and retinal ganglion cell layer, plus olfactory/lateral-line sensory structures; GO supports GPCR/heterotrimeric G-protein signaling typical of sensory neurons [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040718-97), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0007186).
- **ca10a** — expressed in eye and other tissues; supportive of ocular/retinal assignment but not cell-type-specific [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-051030-123).
- **retinal inner nuclear layer** — contains horizontal, bipolar, and amacrine interneurons, matching lhx4 INL expression [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000119).
- **retinal bipolar neuron** — plausible INL subtype, but cluster lacks canonical bipolar markers in the provided list [record](https://www.zfin.org/action/ontology/term/ZFA%3A0009318).

## Caveats
- Markers split across INL/ONL/RGC-layer evidence; no single provided marker definitively selects bipolar vs amacrine vs ganglion/photoreceptor.
- No cycling/progenitor markers are provided; synaptic genes favor mature/quiescent neuron.

**Verdict:** retinal neuron, mature — confidence medium

- **lhx4** — supports retina/neuronal alternative: expressed in nervous system and retina-related studies; ZFIN summary includes adenohypophyseal placode, nervous system, spinal cord neural keel/tube, while a curated publication reports zebrafish retinal ONL/INL expression and roles in retinal neural differentiation [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060728-1), [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-210123-21).
- **ca10a** — broad but eye-compatible: expressed in eye plus cardiovascular/gill/integument/pleuroperitoneal regions; not specific enough for retinal ganglion cell [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-051030-123).
- **calm1a** — neural-supporting but nonspecific calcium transducer; ZFIN expression includes nervous system/neural tube/trigeminal placode, and GO calcium ion binding fits excitable/synaptic cells broadly [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-8308), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0005509).
- **syt5b** — synaptotagmin family marker points toward synaptic vesicle/neurosecretory biology; GO chemical synaptic transmission is consistent with neuronal hypotheses but not cell-type resolving [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0007268).
- **ZFA retina / RGC** — retina is optic-cup-derived neural eye tissue; retinal ganglion cells are neurons whose axons form the optic nerve, matching the gng13b retinal ganglion layer signal [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000152), [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009310).
- **Alternative: olfactory placode/sensory neuron** — gng13b expression in olfactory placode/bulb plus GPCR signaling biology supports this competing sensory-neuron hypothesis [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000048), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0007186).

## Caveats
- No canonical RGC markers such as **atoh7/isl1a** are in the provided list.
- Deepest safe tier: **neural sensory neuron / retinal-olfactory sensory lineage**, not a definitive single cell type.

GO RNA binding is a relevant molecular-function axis for **elavl3/nova2**-type markers [record](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?geneProductId=Q0IHV9&goId=GO%3A0003723). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-080211-1/expression?utm_source=openai))
- **gpm6aa** — ZFIN: expressed in immature eye, nervous system, neural tube; predicted in neuron projection development/regulation of filopodium assembly, active in axonal growth cone/neuronal cell body [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030710-7). GO neuron-projection development is the relevant process [record](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/annotations?geneProductId=Q8AVQ7&goId=GO%3A0031175). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030710-7?utm_source=openai))
- **ptmaa/ptmab** — broad proliferative/chromatin-associated genes; both have nervous-system/CNS expression but also non-neural sites, so they fit “active differentiating neural cells” more than a specific neuron subtype [ptmaa](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-7647), [ptmab](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-8681). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-7647?utm_source=openai))
- **tuba1c** — expressed in nervous system and skeletal muscle; GO-like annotations include microtubule cytoskeleton organization/mitotic cell cycle, so it could reflect neurite growth or cycling, not identity alone [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-061114-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-061114-1?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- Alternative hypothesis: **neural progenitor / differentiating neural precursor**, because **elavl3** includes neuronal stem cell/neural plate/tube expression and **ptmaa/ptmab/tuba1c** can reflect proliferation.
- Deepest defensible tier: **cell type = neuron / neuronal-lineage cell**; not motor, sensory, interneuron, glial, or neural-crest subtype.

**Fin-regeneration blastema / osteogenic mesenchymal progenitor-like cell, progenitor state.**

## Evidence
- **hoxc13a** — expressed in median/ventral fin fold, caudal fin, regenerating fin blastema and osteoblast; supports fin-associated regenerative/osteogenic identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-4/expression). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-4/expression?utm_source=openai))
- **hoxc13b** — curated expression/function literature links this paralog to tail bud and caudal-fin regenerative outgrowth; supports posterior fin/blastema program [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-5). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-5?utm_source=openai))
- **c1qtnf5** — ZFIN expression includes adult caudal-fin amputation blastema, matching a regenerative fin population [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050706-101). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050706-101?utm_source=openai))
- **col1a1a** — extracellular-matrix collagen gene expressed in fin/integument/skeletal system; GO-linked collagen fibril organization and tensile-strength ECM function support mesenchymal/osteogenic matrix production [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9102). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9102?utm_source=openai))
- **crabp2a / rarga** — retinoic-acid binding/receptor markers; GO defines retinoic-acid receptor signaling as nuclear-receptor signaling ending in downstream regulation, consistent with developmental/regenerative patterning [crabp2a](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020320-4), [rarga](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-531), [GO](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0048384). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020320-4?utm_source=openai))
- **blastema** — ZFA defines blastema as proliferative undifferentiated progenitor tissue producing new differentiated structures [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0001270). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001270?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- No canonical macrophage, neural, or epithelial markers are provided; call is driven by fin/blastema + ECM/osteogenic signals.

**Verdict:** fin blastema osteogenic mesenchymal progenitor, progenitor — confidence medium**

## Evidence
- **hoxc13a** — expressed in median/ventral fin fold, post-vent region, tail bud, and regenerating fin blastema/osteoblast; supports posterior fin/axis identity over generic fibroblast. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-4/expression) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-4/expression?utm_source=openai))
- **hoxc13b** — expressed in caudal fin, post-vent region, and tail bud; corroborates caudal fin/posterior identity. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-5) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000822-5?utm_source=openai))
- **col1a1a** — extracellular-matrix/tensile-strength collagen; acts in collagen fibril organization and fin development; expressed in fin, integument, musculature, nervous and skeletal systems. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9102) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9102?utm_source=openai))
- **fbln1** — ECM gene with zebrafish skeletal/osteoblast relevance; favors mesenchymal/osteogenic matrix-producing cells, but is not cell-type-specific alone. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-73) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-73?utm_source=openai))
- **crabp2a / rarga** — retinoic-acid pathway markers: crabp2a is active in retinoic-acid receptor signaling; rarga is expressed in mesoderm/neural crest and pharyngeal/liver-development contexts. [crabp2a](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020320-4), [rarga](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-531), [GO](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0048384) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020320-4?utm_source=openai))
- **ZFA anatomy** — caudal fin is the posterior median fin; ventral fin fold develops into anal and caudal fin. [caudal fin](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001058), [ventral fin fold](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001069) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001058?utm_source=openai))

- **Alternative 2: fin-fold ectoderm/epidermis.** crabp2a literature includes epidermis/fin contexts, and hoxc13 paralogs are fin-fold-associated, but ECM collagen/fibulin pushes toward mesenchymal matrix-producing cells.
- Deepest defensible tier: **posterior fin/fin-fold mesenchymal or osteogenic tissue**, not a precise mature cell type.

**Verdict:** caudal fin-fold/caudal-fin mesenchymal-osteogenic lineage — confidence medium

**Most likely: skeletal muscle myoblast / myogenic progenitor in the myotome, not a fully mature muscle fiber.**

## Evidence
- **myf5** — myogenic regulatory factor; ZFIN-curated publication states it is important for specification/differentiation of muscle cells and expressed in somites, presomitic mesoderm, myotomes, and hypaxial myotomes [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-070122-15).
- **pax7a** — expressed in muscle/myotome and other tissues; paired with **myf5**, this supports a progenitor/satellite-like myogenic identity rather than terminal muscle alone [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-201).
- **thbs4b** — extracellular-matrix/tendon-development-associated gene expressed in musculature system, pectoral fin, trunk, and notochord; compatible with musculoskeletal progenitor niche/ECM context [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020708-4).
- **fabp3** — annotated as “fatty acid binding protein 3, muscle and heart” and expressed in muscle, but adult section data also report ovary/liver expression, so it is supportive but not decisive [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020318-2).
- **alcama** — cell-adhesion gene expressed in musculature system and nervous system; supports developmental/adhesive progenitor context, not specific alone [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-30).
- **myotome** — ZFA defines it as muscle developing from somite and giving rise to body-wall muscle masses [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0001056).
- **skeletal muscle myoblast** — ZFA provides the direct candidate cell/anatomy term [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0009236).
- **MYF5/GO** — GO annotations include skeletal muscle cell differentiation and RNA polymerase II-specific transcription activator/DNA-binding functions, matching myogenic commitment [record](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/P13349/entry).

## Caveats
- **wnt2** and **mdka** are not muscle-specific in ZFIN; they add ambiguity/regenerative-developmental context.
- Lack of terminal sarcomeric markers in the provided list argues against mature fast/slow muscle fiber.

**Verdict:** skeletal muscle myoblast / myogenic progenitor, progenitor — confidence medium**

- **cdon** — ambiguous but compatible: expressed in mesoderm, neural plate/tube and nervous system; mutant/phenotype records implicate slow-twitch muscle development, but also neural crest/Kupffer’s vesicle contexts. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-021115-4?utm_source=openai))
- **fabp3** — alternative hypothesis: cardiac/heart-associated mesoderm, because ZFIN names it “muscle and heart” and links knockdown to cardiac development/heart looping; however adult expression was reported in ovary/liver rather than heart/muscle, and it lacks the paraxial specificity of **myf5**. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020318-2?utm_source=openai))
- **alcama** — alternative neural/cardiac-cell adhesion hypothesis: broad expression includes musculature, nervous system, pericardial region, and curated cardiac-muscle-cell membrane expression; too broad to override **myf5/pax7a**. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-30?utm_source=openai))
- **wnt2** — signaling/mesodermal alternative marker, not cell-type-defining here; curated cardiac-proliferation transgenic context exists, but not enough to call cardiomyocyte without cardiac structural genes. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-416?utm_source=openai))

- Cardiac/pericardial and neural/neural-crest alternatives are real but are driven by broad markers, not the most diagnostic ones.

## Evidence
- **cnn3a** — actin-filament–binding/organization gene expressed in cardiovascular system, **head mesenchyme**, mesoderm and notochord; supports contractile/cytoskeletal mesenchyme rather than a neural identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-5130). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-5130?utm_source=openai))
- **tpm4a** — predicted actin filament binding; expressed in cardiovascular system, **head mesenchyme**, mesoderm and muscle; supports actomyosin-rich mesenchymal/smooth-muscle-like programs but is not cell-type specific [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-2185). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-2185?utm_source=openai))
- **cdh11** — cadherin 11/OB-cadherin; expressed in cleithrum and pectoral fin bud, consistent with skeletal/mesenchymal adhesion programs [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-170). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-170?utm_source=openai))
- **pmp22a** — expressed in head mesenchyme, myotome, pectoral fin and pharyngeal arch; despite myelin-associated name, its curated zebrafish expression overlaps mesenchymal craniofacial/fin tissues here [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-6757). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-6757?utm_source=openai))
- **head mesenchyme** — ZFA defines this as mesoderm plus cranial neural crest contribution giving rise to head connective tissue, bone and musculature [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000113). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000113?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- No canonical fibroblast, neural crest, osteoblast, Schwann-cell, or smooth-muscle marker is provided, so the call should stay broad.
- Markers mix cytoskeletal/adhesion genes and developmental mesenchymal expression; state cannot be assigned.

**Verdict:** head/craniofacial mesenchymal cell — confidence medium

- **cdh11** — argues for adherent mesenchymal/neural/fin-bud contexts rather than pure differentiated muscle; expressed in nervous system, optic vesicle, cleithrum, pectoral fin bud, and linked to cadherin/cell-junction biology. Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely: ECM-producing mesenchymal fibroblast / connective-tissue cell, likely dermal–somitic; state not clearly resolved.**

## Evidence
- **col6a2** — collagen VI ECM gene; expressed in musculature, integument, cardiovascular/digestive structures; GO-linked to muscle development/axonogenesis and predicted extracellular matrix activity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-070501-7).
- **col5a1** — fibrillar collagen; predicted ECM structural constituent and expressed in dermis, dermomyotome, neural crest, notochord, and head [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041105-6).
- **fmoda** — fibromodulin; extracellular-space small leucine-rich proteoglycan family member, expressed in epidermis, periderm, neural crest, and anterior eye segment [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041008-23).
- **postnb** — periostin paralog; predicted extracellular matrix / extracellular-space activity, expressed in epidermis, musculature system, myotome, and somite; acts in muscle attachment [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9120).
- **pdgfrl** — extracellular-region PDGFR-like gene expressed in head mesenchyme, sclerotome, somite, notochord, and cranium, supporting mesenchymal/connective identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-901).
- **GO:0030020** — “extracellular matrix structural constituent conferring tensile strength” fits the collagen-heavy signature [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0030020).
- **ZFA:0000671 horizontal myoseptum** — connective-tissue partition separating epaxial/hypaxial muscle masses; compatible with somite/myoseptal ECM markers [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-641).

## Caveats
- **mdka** can mark quiescent neural stem/radial-glial contexts, but the broader marker set is ECM/mesenchymal, not neural.
- **fabp3** adds muscle/heart/lipid-binding ambiguity, but is not sufficient to call muscle.

**Verdict:** fibroblast-like ECM-producing mesenchymal/connective-tissue cell — confidence medium

## Evidence
- **col5a1** — ECM collagen; expressed in dermis, dermomyotome, neural crest, notochord; GO supports tensile-strength ECM structural constituent → strongest fibroblast/mesenchyme signal. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041105-6?utm_source=openai))
- **col6a2** — collagen VI; expressed across musculature, integument, cardiovascular and digestive systems; GO/ZFIN notes extracellular-matrix activity plus muscle development, fitting stromal/perimysial ECM rather than a specific differentiated cell type. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-070501-7?utm_source=openai))
- **postnb** — periostin ortholog; expressed in epidermis, musculature system, myotome and somite; acts in muscle attachment and is predicted active in extracellular matrix/extracellular space → supports connective tissue at muscle/skin interfaces. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9120?utm_source=openai))
- **fabp3** — argues for an alternative: cardiac/lipid-metabolic or liver-associated identity; ZFIN lists expression in muscle, nervous system, pharyngeal arch and pleuroperitoneal region, and publications link it to cardiac development and hepatic steatosis, but it is not enough to override the collagen/periostin ECM program. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020318-2?utm_source=openai))
- **mdka** — ambiguous: can mark activated hepatic stellate cells during liver regeneration and adult telencephalic radial glia after injury; here, with collagens/postnb, it favors activated stromal biology more than neural identity. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-240828-2?utm_source=openai))
- ZFA anatomy tier: **integument/dermis** and **somite/myotome** are defensible tissues, but no provided marker uniquely pins a mature zebrafish fibroblast subtype. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000368?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- Deepest safe call is **mesenchymal/stromal ECM-producing cell**, not a named fibroblast subtype.
- Alternative hypotheses: **muscle-associated connective tissue** > **cardiac/hepatic activated stromal cell**; mature cardiomyocyte or myocyte is weak.

**Verdict:** mesenchymal stromal / fibroblast-like ECM-producing cell, mature or activated — confidence medium

**Most defensible call: cycling/proliferative neural-lineage cell, not a resolved mature neuronal subtype.**

## Evidence
- **mki67** — canonical proliferation marker; ZFIN names it “marker of proliferation Ki-67” and predicts involvement in regulation of mitotic nuclear division; expressed in several embryonic structures. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9771)
- **mki67** — GO support: UniProt/GO annotates zebrafish Mki67 to “regulation of mitotic nuclear division,” supporting a cycling state. [record](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A0A8M1NZY3/entry)
- **hmgb2a** — chromatin/DNA-binding high-mobility-group gene; ZFIN reports expression in central nervous system, gut, neuromast, ovary, and pectoral fin bud, so it supports proliferative/chromatin activity but is not lineage-specific. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-051120-126)
- **hmgn2** — predicted chromatin-binding/chromatin-organization nuclear factor; consistent with proliferating, chromatin-active cells, but ZFIN expression is not cell-type resolving. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-051030-81)
- **hmga1a** — predicted AT-rich DNA binding/transcription coregulator; ZFIN reports expression in nervous system and otic vesicle among other sites. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-010502-1)
- **tubb4b/tubb4bb** — current ZFIN symbol is **tubb4bb**; expressed in brain and predicted as cytoskeletal/microtubule component, compatible with neural context but not sufficient for neuron subtype identity. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-8625)
- **ZFA nervous system** — consists of neurons and neuroglial cells, divided into CNS and PNS; this fits the weak neural-expression evidence but does not identify a specific cell class. [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000396)

## Caveats
- No provided markers are definitive mature neuron, glial, neural crest, or retinal progenitor markers.
- The strongest signal is cell-cycle/chromatin, so over-calling a specific neural subtype would be unsafe.

**Verdict:** proliferative neural-lineage cell, cycling — confidence medium**

- **desma** — desmin intermediate filament; expressed in musculature, somite, skeletal muscle/myocardium and tied to sarcomere organization [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-221). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-221?utm_source=openai))
- **cav3** — sarcolemmal caveolin; expressed in adaxial cell/heart/musculature and annotated to muscle cell fate commitment, striated muscle differentiation, myoblast fusion, and sarcomere organization [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050522-426). ([uniprot.org](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/A4VAK4/entry?utm_source=openai))
- **hsp90aa1.1** — expressed in musculature/paraxial mesoderm/skeletal muscle myoblast; involved in myofibril assembly and unfolded-protein binding → stress/proteostasis support [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-94). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-94?utm_source=openai))

**Fast skeletal muscle cell / fast muscle fiber, mature contractile state.**

## Evidence
- **myhz2** — fast-muscle-specific myosin heavy chain; expressed in musculature system, trunk, pharyngeal arch and fin; GO implicates skeletal muscle fiber development and myosin motor activity [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020604-1).  
- **myhz2** — publication record describes an embryonic/tail muscle-specific MHC with similarity to carp fast skeletal MHC and trunk/tail expression [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-021106-8).  
- **tnni2a.4** — fast skeletal troponin I; mutant phenotype disrupts fast muscle cell myofibrils, sarcomere organization, and striated muscle cell development [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-040625-119/phenotype-summary).  
- **tnnt3a** — troponin T perturbation causes fast muscle cell actin-filament and myofibril abnormalities, supporting sarcomeric fast-muscle identity [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-000322-3/phenotype-summary).  
- **actc1b** — actin expressed in musculature system and trunk; widely used as an actc1b-driven muscle reporter context [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000322-1).  
- **fast muscle cell** — ZFA term is a muscle cell with fast contractile response; synonymous with fast muscle fiber/white muscle cell, deep myotome [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009117).  
- **sarcomere organization** — GO term matches the actomyosin/troponin program: organization of muscle actomyosin into sarcomeres [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0045214).

**Verdict:** fast skeletal muscle cell, mature — confidence high

**Fast skeletal muscle / myotomal myofiber, mature — contractile sarcomere markers strongly support differentiated fast muscle.**

## Evidence
- **myhz1.2** — skeletal myosin heavy-chain gene; expressed in cephalic musculature and trunk, and predicted active in myofibril/myosin filament → contractile skeletal muscle identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-070705-73).
- **tnni2b.2** — fast skeletal troponin I; expressed in adaxial cell, cephalic musculature, muscle, myotome and somite; predicted involved in skeletal muscle contraction and troponin complex [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040801-9).
- **tnnt3b** — fast skeletal troponin T; expressed in musculature system and somite, acts in sarcomere organization, predicted troponin complex component [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030520-2).
- **mylpfb** — fast skeletal myosin light-chain; expressed in mesoderm, musculature system and somite; predicted involved in actin–myosin filament sliding and skeletal muscle tissue development [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040912-115).
- **pvalb2 / pvalb1** — parvalbumins with curated expression in somite/myotome/musculature system, consistent with muscle calcium handling [pvalb2](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000322-4), [pvalb1](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-57).
- ZFA anatomy support: expression localizes to **myotome / musculature system**, appropriate for zebrafish skeletal myofibers [myotome record](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ols4/ontologies/zfa/classes/http%253A%252F%252Fpurl.obolibrary.org%252Fobo%252FZFA_0009288?lang=en).
- GO support: marker functions converge on **skeletal muscle contraction** and sarcomeric actin–myosin force generation [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0003009).

## Caveats
- **si:ch73-367p23.2** has no curated expression/GO support, so it is not identity-informative.

**Most likely identity: skeletal muscle cell / skeletal muscle fiber, mature contractile state.**

## Evidence
- **acta1a** — skeletal actin; expressed in trunk skeletal muscle, head/extraocular musculature, pectoral fin/fold, and hypaxial muscle; acts in skeletal muscle fiber development [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050417-267), [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-FIG-180620-14).
- **tnni1c** — slow skeletal troponin I; predicted actin binding, troponin complex membership, and involvement in skeletal/cardiac muscle contraction [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060825-192).
- **myl10** — myosin light chain with curated embryonic expression in somite/adaxial cells and later fast and slow muscle cells; also reported in heart, so not fully skeletal-specific [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050417-421/expression).
- **tpm2** — tropomyosin; predicted actin-filament binding, muscle contraction, and actin filament organization; located in striated muscle thin filament and expressed in musculature system/somite [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-114).
- **tnnc1b** — troponin C marker with curated expression in skeletal muscle [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-62/expression).
- **ZFA skeletal muscle cell** — appears from segmentation and persists to adult; synonymized with skeletal muscle fiber / striated muscle cell [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009115). **ZFA skeletal muscle** is muscle of long multinucleated cells attached via tendons [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0005277).
- **GO support** — troponin complex is part of striated muscle thin filament and regulates contraction; muscle contraction is force generation in muscle tissue via actin–myosin activity [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0005861), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0006936).

## Caveats
- **tnnt2c** is named cardiac troponin T2c, but ZFIN phenotype links it to striated muscle/myofibril development; without cardiac-enriched markers, skeletal muscle is more defensible [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-110124-2).
- Fast vs slow subtype is unresolved: markers include both slow-associated and broader contractile muscle genes.

**Verdict:** skeletal muscle fiber, mature — confidence high

## Evidence
- **tnnt2c** — “cardiac” troponin T ortholog, but curated expression is mesoderm/musculature system/somite/trunk mesenchyme, not uniquely heart; supports striated muscle, not decisive cardiomyocyte [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030520-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030520-1?utm_source=openai))
- **acta1a** — skeletal α-actin; acts in skeletal muscle fiber development and is expressed in adaxial cell, musculature system, trunk, fin/pericardial regions [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050417-267). ZFIN figure curation specifically reports trunk skeletal muscle, ocular/head musculature, pectoral fin/fold, hypaxial muscle [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-FIG-180620-14). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050417-267?utm_source=openai))
- **tnni1c** — slow skeletal troponin I; predicted in both skeletal and cardiac muscle contraction, so it weighs toward slow/striated muscle but does not separate heart from somite [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060825-192). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060825-192?utm_source=openai))
- **tnnc1b** — slow/cardiac troponin C; expressed in adaxial cell, heart, musculature system and somite, with curated expression including slow muscle cell and cardiac muscle cell [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-62), making it the main ambiguity driver. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-62?utm_source=openai))
- **myl13** — myosin light chain expressed in adaxial cell, heart, musculature system and somite; supports striated muscle, not a specific branch [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-1593). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-1593?utm_source=openai))
- ZFA supports both hypotheses: slow muscle cell is a zebrafish muscle-cell term appearing from early segmentation [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009116), while cardiac muscle is heart muscle composed of cardiac muscle cells [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0005280). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009116?utm_source=openai))
- GO matches a sarcomeric contractile program: troponin complex regulates muscle contraction [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0005861); skeletal muscle contraction and cardiac muscle contraction are separate compatible processes [records](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0003009), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0060048). ([amigo.geneontology.org](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0005861?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- **Alternative hypothesis:** cardiomyocyte/cardiac muscle cell, driven by tnnt2c/tnnc1b/myl13 heart associations, but lack of classic heart-only markers in the provided list prevents a confident cell-type call.
- Deepest defensible tier: **striated muscle cell / muscle tissue**; skeletal slow muscle is favored over cardiomyocyte by acta1a and somite/adaxial expression.

**Verdict:** striated muscle cell, mature — confidence medium**

If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely: slow skeletal muscle cell / slow muscle fiber, mature contractile state.**

## Evidence
- **smyhc1** — slow-fiber myosin; mutant evidence specifically disrupts slow-muscle sarcomeres and labeling, supporting slow skeletal muscle identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-200110-5).
- **tnnc1b** — expressed in slow muscle cell, somite slow muscle cell, trunk musculature slow muscle cell, plus heart; with this marker set it supports slow/striated muscle rather than heart alone [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-62/expression).
- **myl10** — expressed in adaxial cell, slow muscle cell, somite, and heart; reinforces slow-muscle/adaxial lineage signal [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050417-421).
- **tpm3** — expressed in adaxial cell, slow muscle cell, myotome and musculature system; acts in skeletal myofibril assembly [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030826-16).
- **tnnt2d** — troponin T family gene expressed in myotome and somite; predicted in troponin complex and sarcomere organization [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050626-97).
- **pvalb4** — calcium-binding parvalbumin expressed in musculature system, myotome, and pectoral fin musculature [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-48).
- **slow muscle cell** — ZFA term is “slow muscle fiber/red muscle cell,” a muscle cell with high lipid/mitochondrial content [record](https://zfin.org/action/ontology/term/ZFA%3A0009116).
- **skeletal myofibril assembly** — GO process describes maturation/formation of skeletal-muscle myofibrils, matching the troponin/myosin/tropomyosin program [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0014866).

## Caveats
- Some markers are also cardiac/striated-muscle genes, but **smyhc1 + tpm3 + tnnc1b + myl10** favor slow skeletal muscle.

**Verdict:** slow skeletal muscle cell, mature — confidence high

## Evidence
- **smyhc1** — strongest discriminator: slow myosin heavy chain; mutant/phenotype records repeatedly implicate slow muscle cell sarcomere/Z-disc defects, supporting slow skeletal myofiber over heart [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-030131-271/phenotype-summary).
- **tnni4b.2** — curated WT expression includes somite slow muscle cell, trunk/cephalic musculature, and pectoral fin; this directly supports skeletal slow muscle [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-81/wt-expression).
- **tnnc1b** — ambiguous: ZFIN describes cardiac contraction and expression in heart, but also adaxial cell, somite, musculature system, and curated slow muscle cell expression; supports muscle, not uniquely cardiac [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-62).
- **tnnt2d** — “cardiac” troponin T paralog, but ZFIN expression is myotome/somite and GO-style function is sarcomere organization/troponin complex, weighing toward striated skeletal context here [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050626-97).
- **pvalb4** — calcium-binding parvalbumin expressed in musculature system, myotome, and pectoral fin musculature; corroborates skeletal muscle [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-48).
- **myl10** — expressed in adaxial cell, somite, slow muscle cell, and heart; again mixed but compatible with slow muscle lineage [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050417-421).
- ZFA/ontology support: “slow muscle cell” is the deepest defensible cell-type tier because multiple markers map to curated slow muscle/somite anatomy; GO “sarcomere organization” supports mature contractile striated muscle rather than progenitor [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0045214).

## Caveats
- **Alternative hypothesis:** cardiomyocyte/cardiac muscle cell, driven by **tnnc1b**, **tnnt2d**, **myl10** heart annotations. It loses to slow skeletal muscle because **smyhc1** and **tnni4b.2** are slow-skeletal/somite-weighted.
- I would not defend below “slow skeletal muscle cell / slow-twitch myofiber” subtype without more markers.

**Verdict:** slow skeletal muscle cell, mature — confidence high

**Most likely: differentiating skeletal muscle myoblast / nascent myofiber, likely myogenic differentiation rather than mature quiescent muscle.**

## Evidence
- **myog** — myogenin is expressed in musculature/myoblast and acts in positive regulation of myoblast fusion and skeletal muscle regeneration; GO supports myoblast fusion as a myogenic differentiation process [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-265). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-265?utm_source=openai))
- **rbm24a** — expressed in adaxial cells, fast/slow muscle cells, somite and cephalic musculature; involved in striated muscle tissue development and sarcomere organization [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040628-1/expression). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040628-1/expression?utm_source=openai))
- **mef2d** — expressed in adaxial cell, fast muscle myoblast and musculature system; supports skeletal muscle myosin thick-filament assembly [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-164). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-164?utm_source=openai))
- **jam2a** — expressed in myoblast/musculature and acts positively on myoblast fusion, matching GO myoblast-fusion biology [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-031204-3). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-031204-3?utm_source=openai))
- **hsp90aa1.1** — expressed in paraxial mesoderm, skeletal muscle myoblast and musculature; involved in myofibril assembly, suggesting nascent contractile apparatus/chaperone demand [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-94). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-94?utm_source=openai))
- **ZFA anchor** — somite/myotomal skeletal muscle context is supported by ZFIN anatomy-linked expression for myog/rbm24a [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0000155). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000155?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- Heat-shock markers may reflect proteostasis stress, but core myogenic markers dominate.
- Fast vs slow fiber subtype is not definitive from these markers alone.

**Verdict:** skeletal muscle myoblast / nascent myofiber, mature — confidence high**

- **rbm24a** — supports striated muscle but is not specific: expressed in adaxial cell, fast muscle cell, slow muscle cell, somite, heart and sensory structures; GO/ZFIN functions include sarcomere organization and striated muscle tissue development. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040628-1/expression) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040628-1/expression?utm_source=openai))
- **mef2d** — supports myoblast/nascent muscle: expressed in adaxial cell, fast muscle myoblast and musculature system; acts in skeletal muscle myosin thick-filament assembly. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-164) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-164?utm_source=openai))
- **hsp90aa1.1** — compatible with muscle differentiation/stress-chaperone biology: expressed in musculature system, paraxial mesoderm and skeletal muscle myoblast; acts in myofibril assembly. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-94) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-94?utm_source=openai))
- **fast muscle myoblast** — ZFA defines this as a skeletal muscle myoblast that differentiates into fast muscle fibers, matching myog/mef2d/rbm24a better than a fully mature fiber. [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0009369) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009369?utm_source=openai))
- **Alternative: mature fast muscle cell** — plausible because rbm24a is detected in fast muscle cell and ZFA defines fast muscle cells as fast-contracting myotome fibers, but the marker set lacks stronger structural fast-fiber markers here. [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0009117) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009117?utm_source=openai))
- **Alternative: cardiac or sensory lineage** — rbm24a and hsp90aa1.1 have heart/sensory-associated expression, but **myog** is a skeletal myogenic determinant, making these less likely as primary identities. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040628-1/expression) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040628-1/expression?utm_source=openai))

- No down-regulated markers were provided, so exclusion of cardiac/sensory alternatives is incomplete.
- Deepest defensible tier: **skeletal myogenic cell**, probably **fast muscle myoblast / differentiating myoblast**, not confidently mature fast fiber.

- **tnni2a.4** — fast skeletal troponin I duplicate; expressed in musculature system/somite, part of troponin complex; mutant phenotype disrupts fast muscle-cell myofibrils/sarcomeres [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-119). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-119?utm_source=openai))

([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040625-57?utm_source=openai))

- **GO sarcomere organization** — organization of actomyosin into sarcomeres in muscle cells matches the troponin/myosin/tropomyosin program [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0045214). ([amigo.geneontology.org](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0045214?utm_source=openai))

Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely identity: cardiac muscle cell / cardiomyocyte, mature contractile state.**

## Evidence
- **cmlc1** — cardiac myosin light chain; expressed in cardiac muscle myoblast/heart primordium and acts in heart contraction/myofibril assembly [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030522-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030522-1?utm_source=openai))
- **myl7** — canonical cardiac myosin light-chain marker with cardiovascular-system expression and heart contractility phenotypes [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-991019-3). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-991019-3?utm_source=openai))
- **tnnt2a** — cardiac troponin T; expressed in cardiac muscle/heart/cardiac ventricle and part of troponin complex [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000626-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000626-1?utm_source=openai))
- **tpm4a** — tropomyosin; acts in cardiac muscle contraction and cardiac myofibril assembly; expressed in cardiovascular system/muscle [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-2185). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-2185?utm_source=openai))
- **tnni1b** — cardiac troponin I–linked locus; reported as heart-expressed during early cardiogenesis and tied to myocardial/atrioventricular valve development [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-180726-6). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-180726-6?utm_source=openai))
- **tnnc1a** — troponin C; acts in cardiac muscle contraction/ventricle development and is predicted in cardiac troponin complex [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030523-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030523-1?utm_source=openai))
- **ZFA/CL anatomy** — “cardiac muscle cell” is the ZFA cardiomyocyte term; CL defines it as a striated muscle cell responsible for heart contraction [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009316). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009316?utm_source=openai))
- **GO** — the marker set converges on cardiac muscle contraction and troponin complex biology [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0060048). ([amigo.geneontology.org](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0060048?utm_source=openai))

**Verdict:** cardiac muscle cell / cardiomyocyte, mature — confidence high

## Evidence
- **myl7** — curated as expressed in heart/cardiac muscle contexts, with ZFIN anatomy pages listing **myl7** among top genes for both atrial and ventricular myocardium; this strongly supports cardiomyocyte rather than generic muscle ([record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-991019-3)). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-991019-3?utm_source=openai))
- **tnnt2a** — “troponin T type 2a (cardiac)”; ZFIN says it is expressed in cardiac muscle/cardiovascular system/mesoderm, and GO places the implicated process as cardiac muscle contraction ([record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000626-1)). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000626-1?utm_source=openai))
- **cmlc1** — ZFIN anatomy links **cmlc1** to cardiac muscle myoblast/cardioblast, supporting cardiac lineage; however myoblast annotation alone would not prove progenitor state without earlier-stage markers ([record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030522-1)). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030522-1?utm_source=openai))
- **tpm4a** — expressed in cardiovascular system and muscle; GO/ZFIN summary says it acts in cardiac muscle contraction and cardiac myofibril assembly, supporting contractile myocardium but not alone cell-type-specific ([record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-2185)). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-2185?utm_source=openai))
- **tnni1b** — slow skeletal troponin I ortholog and expressed in musculature plus cardiovascular system; this is the main reason for the alternative **skeletal/striated muscle** hypothesis, but it also acts in heart development ([record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041212-37)). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041212-37?utm_source=openai))
- **ZFA anatomy** — cardiac muscle is “muscle composed of cardiac muscle cells that is part of the heart,” while skeletal muscle is a separate long cylindrical multinucleated muscle category; the marker set is much more cardiac-enriched because of **myl7/tnnt2a/cmlc1** ([record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0005280)). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0005280?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- **tpm4a/tnni1b/tnnc1a** are striated-muscle/sarcomere-compatible, so the deepest safe fallback would be **mesoderm-derived striated muscle**, but cardiac markers make cardiomyocyte more defensible.
- No cycling/progenitor markers are provided; “mature-contractile” is inferred from sarcomere/contraction genes, not proven by cell-cycle absence.

**Verdict:** cardiomyocyte / cardiac muscle cell, mature — confidence high

Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most defensible call: embryonic mesodermal progenitor, with weak bias toward intermediate/pronephric-field rather than a mature cell type.**

## Evidence
- **lhx1a** — LIM-homeobox TF; current records link it to kidney/regeneration studies, and its curated gene record supports developmental regulatory identity rather than mature differentiated fate [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-347).
- **pitx2** — homeobox TF expressed in multiple embryonic structures including **mesoderm**; GO-linked description includes DNA-binding TF activity and developmental processes [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990714-27).
- **ptk7a** — expressed in head, neural tube, somite and tail bud; GO-linked roles include Wnt/planar-cell-polarity signaling and morphogenesis, consistent with early morphogenetic progenitors, not a terminal lineage [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050522-216).
- **qkia** — RNA-binding gene expressed in mesoderm, musculature, nervous system and heart tube; broad developmental expression supports an immature/progenitor-like annotation [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-230).
- **aif1l** — actin/calcium-associated gene expressed in fin, nervous system, periderm and eye; supportive of cytoskeletal/remodeling state but not diagnostic for immune/macrophage identity here [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9646).
- **intermediate mesoderm** — ZFA term appears from bud to Prim-5 and is the embryonic field that gives rise to kidney/gonad lineages [record](https://zfin.org/action/anatomy/anatomy-view/ZFA%3A0001206); GO “intermediate mesoderm development” explicitly defines this field as developing into kidney and gonads [record](https://zfin.org/GO%3A0048389).
- **pronephric duct** — plausible downstream renal structure, but the provided markers lack strong canonical duct markers; ZFA defines it as embryonic kidney duct [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000150).

## Caveats
- No strong mature epithelial, neural, muscle, blood, or immune marker dominates.
- “Intermediate/pronephric” is suggested mainly by **lhx1a/pitx2** context, not proven.

**Verdict:** mesodermal progenitor, progenitor — confidence medium-low**

## Evidence
- **ptk7a** — supports an early morphogenesis/progenitor hypothesis: expressed in neural tube, somite, tail bud, head; GO-linked to Wnt/planar-cell-polarity and notochord morphogenesis. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050522-216) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050522-216?utm_source=openai))
- **lhx1a** — strongly early developmental: expressed in germ ring, mesoderm, nervous system, neural rod, renal system; GO annotations include embryonic morphogenesis, generation of neurons, kidney development. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-347) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-347?utm_source=openai))
- **pitx2** — compatible with head/mesodermal and neural developmental domains, but broad: expressed in brain, head, digestive system, dental epithelium, mesoderm; involved in eye, left-right, nervous-system development. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990714-27) ([zfin.org](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990714-27?utm_source=openai))
- **qkia** — alternative neural/glial or muscle-development angle: expressed in neural head tissue and paraxial mesoderm; GO includes RNA binding, regulation of astrocyte differentiation, skeletal muscle tissue development. [record](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/Q6P0D0) ([uniprot.org](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/Q6P0D0?utm_source=openai))
- **aif1l / tmsb** — argue against a clean neural-only call: aif1l is periderm/fin/nervous-system and actin/ruffle-associated; tmsb is integument/gill/liver/thymus and wound/inflammatory-response-related. [aif1l](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9646), [tmsb](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050307-5) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9646?utm_source=openai))
- Anatomy support: candidate tiers include **mesoderm** and **neural tube**, but ZFA defines these as broad embryonic structures, not specific cell types. [mesoderm](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000041), [neural tube](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001135) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000041?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- **Alternative 1: neural tube/neural progenitor** — supported by ptk7a, lhx1a, qkia, pitx2; weakened by mesoderm/renal/periderm/inflammatory markers.
- **Alternative 2: mesodermal/renal or paraxial progenitor** — supported by lhx1a, pitx2, qkia, ptk7a; weakened by lack of more specific provided renal/somite markers.
- Deepest defensible tier: **embryonic tissue/germ-layer-associated progenitor**, not a named mature cell type.

**Verdict:** embryonic mesoderm/neuroectoderm-associated progenitor-like population, progenitor — confidence medium

Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most defensible call: erythroid/hematopoietic cell, likely mature erythrocyte-like, but ambiguous because several markers are broad mesoderm/epithelial/cytoskeletal genes.**

## Evidence
- **rhag** — strongest lineage clue: expressed in cardiovascular and hematopoietic systems; predicted ammonium channel/urea transport fits Rh-family erythroid membrane biology [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-8229); GO supports ammonium transmembrane transport [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0072488).
- **tmsb4x** — expressed in heart/heart tube/lateral plate mesoderm and adult epicardium cell, supporting mesodermal/cardiovascular context rather than a specific erythroid-only identity [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-030131-8304/expression); GO actin-monomer binding supports a cytoskeletal/regenerative state marker, not lineage specificity [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0003785?relation=regulates).
- **tmem88b** — expressed in lateral plate mesoderm and pharyngeal endoderm; acts negatively on canonical Wnt signaling/endodermal fate, so it does not cleanly specify erythroid fate [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060929-644).
- **cavin2b** — expressed in epidermis/periderm/hypochord/nervous system; caveola/cytoplasm annotation is not erythroid-specific, weakening the call [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040912-149).
- **pcolcea** — extracellular collagen-processing enhancer with no curated wild-type expression in ZFIN; suggests matrix/mesenchymal context but is not decisive [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041014-370).
- ZFA support: hematopoietic system is the zebrafish system generating hematopoietic cells [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0005023); erythrocyte is the red blood cell term [record](https://www.zfin.org/action/ontology/term/CL%3A0000232).

## Caveats
- No canonical erythroid transcription/hemoglobin marker was provided.
- tmsb4x/tmem88b/cavin2b point to cardiovascular/mesodermal or epithelial contexts, so this could be a mixed/transition cluster.

**Verdict:** erythroid/hematopoietic cell, mature — confidence medium-low

**Most defensible call: cardiovascular/pharyngeal mesendodermal cluster, not a clean mature cell type; endothelial/vascular-support is the leading hypothesis, with pharyngeal endoderm/progenitor and erythroid/gill ionocyte alternatives.**

## Evidence
- **ftr82** — strongest pro-vascular marker: reported during vessel development; loss disrupts ISV/CVP growth and angiogenesis, supporting endothelial/vascular identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-170119-3). ZFA pharyngeal/branchial vasculature is a defined tubular fluid-transport structure [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0005003).  
- **tmsb4x** — supports cardiovascular/mesothelial context: expressed in lateral plate mesoderm, heart rudiment/tube, and adult epicardium cell [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-030131-8304/expression). ZFA ventricular epicardium is a mesothelial external ventricular layer [record](https://zfin.org/action/ontology/term/ZFA:0005058). GO implicates actin-monomer binding/cytoskeletal regulation, compatible with motile vascular/mesothelial cells [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-8304).  
- **tmem88b** — alternative pharyngeal endoderm/progenitor hypothesis: expressed in lateral plate mesoderm and pharyngeal endoderm; acts negatively on canonical Wnt signaling and in endodermal cell fate specification [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-060929-644). ZFA pharyngeal endoderm is a defined embryonic anatomy term [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-1064); GO canonical Wnt signaling supports developmental-patterning interpretation [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0060070).  
- **rhag** — erythroid/gill alternative: expressed in cardiovascular, hematopoietic, and gill structures; GO ammonium transport fits gas/ion-transport epithelia or blood-associated cells [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-8229), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0072488).  
- **pcolcea/cavin2b/actb2** — broad ECM/cytoskeletal/epithelial support, not decisive: pcolcea has collagen/ECM functions but no curated WT expression [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041014-370); cavin2b is epidermis/periderm/hypochord/nervous-system expressed [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040912-149); actb2 is broadly expressed [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000329-3).

## Caveats
- No provided canonical endothelial markers, erythroid globins, or pharyngeal endoderm markers besides **tmem88b**.
- Deepest defensible tier: **cardiovascular/pharyngeal developmental tissue**, not a specific mature cell type.

**Verdict:** cardiovascular/pharyngeal mesendoderm-associated cell, progenitor/immature — confidence medium-low

**Most likely: pharyngeal-arch / branchiomeric mesodermal muscle progenitor-like cells, with a weak growth/protein-homeostasis state.**

## Evidence
- **gfra3** — expressed in **pharyngeal arch**, pharyngeal arch 1/2, hyoid muscle, and pharyngeal musculature; acts in branchiomeric skeletal muscle development [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-110512-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-110512-1?utm_source=openai))
- **tbx1** — expressed in mesoderm, cardiovascular system, vestibuloauditory system, and **pharyngeal arch**; acts in chordate pharyngeal muscle development and secondary heart-field cardioblast proliferation [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030805-5). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030805-5?utm_source=openai))
- **pharyngeal arch** — ZFA term describes paired arches with mesodermal and neural-crest contributions along the foregut, appearing from 10–13 somites [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001306). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001306?utm_source=openai))
- **npm1a** — nucleolar RNA/chromatin/histone-binding factor expressed in hematopoietic cell and many embryonic structures; supports biosynthetic/progenitor-like activity, not lineage identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-021028-1). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-021028-1?utm_source=openai))
- **ran** — GTPase/GTP-binding gene expressed in multiple tissues including splanchnocranium; generic growth/transport signal rather than specific identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-88). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-88?utm_source=openai))
- **hsp90ab1** — ATP-dependent chaperone expressed in head/eye; may indicate protein-homeostasis/stress, but not enough alone to call “stress” [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-95). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-95?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- No canonical cartilage/neural-crest marker is provided, so I would not call chondrocyte or cranial neural crest.
- State is suggestive only; cycling markers are weak/non-specific.

**ECM-secreting fibroblast / connective-tissue stromal cell, likely myoseptal–skeletal associated.**

## Evidence
- **postnb** — extracellular-matrix/adhesion gene; expressed in epidermis, musculature system, myotome and somite; acts in muscle attachment [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9120). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9120?utm_source=openai))

- **matn4** — predicted extracellular-matrix protein; expressed in integument, skeletal system and vertical myoseptum [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050208-64). Vertical myoseptum is connective tissue between myotomes [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0000610). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050208-64?utm_source=openai))
- **tgfbi** — predicted ECM/extracellular-space activity; expressed in head mesenchyme, neural crest cell, paraxial mesoderm and splanchnocranium [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-73). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-73?utm_source=openai))
- **sparc** — osteonectin/matricellular ECM gene; expressed in cranium, pectoral fin, hematopoietic system and vestibuloauditory system; functions in pharyngeal system development [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9?utm_source=openai))
- **tmem119b** — predicted positive regulation of osteoblast differentiation/proliferation and bone mineralization, supporting skeletal stromal identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-070410-49). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-070410-49?utm_source=openai))
- ZFA **fibroblast** is “a connective tissue cell which secretes an extracellular matrix rich in collagen and other macromolecules” [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-2084); GO **extracellular matrix organization** matches the shared ECM program [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0030198). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-2084?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- No single marker uniquely distinguishes fibroblast from perichondrial/osteogenic stromal cells.
- **vwde** has no curated ZFIN expression, so it adds weak support only.

## Evidence
- **postnb** — strongest “osteoblast-like” clue by name, but curated zebrafish expression is broad ECM/connective: epidermis, musculature, myotome, somite; not a clean osteoblast-only marker. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9120))
- **matn4** — extracellular-matrix gene expressed in skeletal system, hypochord, integument, nervous system, and vertical myoseptum; supports ECM/skeletal connective tissue but not a single cell type. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050208-64))
- **tgfbi** — ECM/extracellular-space gene expressed in head mesenchyme, neural crest cell, paraxial mesoderm, and splanchnocranium; this weighs toward cranial/mesenchymal connective tissue. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-73))
- **sparc** — osteonectin/ECM-associated, expressed in cranium, hematopoietic system, pectoral fin/bud, and vestibuloauditory system; supports skeletogenic/ECM but creates ambiguity with ear/hematopoietic contexts. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-9))
- **tmem119b** — predicted positive regulator of osteoblast differentiation/proliferation/mineralization, but ZFIN expression includes blood island, vasculature, spinal cord, tail bud, and cultured adult brain. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-070410-49?utm_source=openai))
- **ZFA anatomy** — “osteoblast” is a bone-forming ECM-secreting cell, fitting the ECM/mineralization theme; “chondrocyte” forms cartilage and remains an alternative because matn4/sparc/tgfbi overlap skeletal/cartilage-associated contexts. ([zfin.org](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-2089?utm_source=openai))
- **GO** — the shared signal is best captured as extracellular matrix organization, not a lineage-exclusive program. ([amigo.geneontology.org](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0030198?utm_source=openai))

## Alternatives weighed
- **Osteoblast / bone-forming cell:** supported by postnb name, tmem119b osteoblast predictions, ECM secretion, skeletal expression.
- **Chondrocyte / cranial cartilage-associated cell:** plausible from matn4/sparc/tgfbi cranial–skeletal ECM expression, but lacks canonical chondrocyte markers in the provided list.
- **General mesenchymal fibroblast-like ECM cell:** deepest defensible tier; ZFA mesenchyme is a less-compact mesh-like cell arrangement, and head mesenchyme gives rise to connective tissue, bone, and musculature. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000393?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- No provided marker is lineage-exclusive; several are broad ECM genes.
- Without down-regulated markers or canonical osteoblast/chondrocyte markers, I would not force a mature cell-type label.

**Verdict:** mesenchymal ECM-producing skeletogenic/connective-tissue cell — confidence medium

Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely: lbx1⁺ spinal cord neural progenitor / interneuron lineage, with heat-shock/mitochondrial stress signature — ambiguous vs migratory muscle precursor.**

## Evidence
- **lbx1a** — homeobox TF; ZFIN reports expression in nervous system plus anterior migratory muscle precursor stream and muscle, so it supports an lbx-lineage call but not a single tissue alone [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040724-40). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040724-40))
- **lbx1b** — paralogous LBX TF; ZFIN reports expression in nervous system, neural plate/tube, and spinal cord neural keel; curated publication summary notes lbx1b expression in spinal cord progenitor cells [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050309-27). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050309-27?utm_source=openai))
- **lbx1a/lbx1b context** — mutant expression summaries involve spinal cord inhibitory/glycinergic interneuron markers, supporting an interneuron-lineage interpretation rather than mature muscle alone [record](https://zfin.org/action/expression/fish-expression-figure-summary?fishID=ZDB-FISH-241106-6&imagesOnly=false). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/action/expression/fish-expression-figure-summary?fishID=ZDB-FISH-241106-6&imagesOnly=false&utm_source=openai))
- **spinal cord interneuron** — ZFA has a spinal cord interneuron anatomy term, consistent with the lbx-linked spinal lineage [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA:0000778). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000778?utm_source=openai))
- **hspe1 / hspd1** — mitochondrial chaperonin/co-chaperonin markers; hspe1 is annotated for protein-folding chaperone binding and protein folding, suggesting a stress/proteostasis state rather than identity [hspe1](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000906-2), [GO term](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0051087/). ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000906-2?utm_source=openai))
- **calm1b** — calmodulin supports Ca²⁺ signaling broadly, including neural excitability, but is not cell-type-specific [record](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q6PI52/entry). ([uniprot.org](https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q6PI52/entry?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- **pitx2**, **c1qbp**, **hspe1**, and **lbx1a** also have mesoderm/muscle or broad developmental expression, so “spinal interneuron progenitor” is not definitive.
- No mature neurotransmitter marker is in the provided list.

**Verdict:** lbx1⁺ spinal cord interneuron progenitor, stress — confidence medium

Independent second read (alternative-hypothesis pass) for the same cluster:

**Most defensible call: embryonic lbx-positive neuromuscular/developmental population; deepest safe tier = neural tube/spinal cord–hindbrain vs migratory muscle precursor, not a single mature cell type.**

## Evidence
- **lbx1a** — Strongest clue: expressed in nervous system, hindbrain neural plate, muscle, pectoral fin, and anterior migratory muscle precursor stream; GO-style function is DNA-binding RNA-pol-II TF activity, so this marks developmental fate specification rather than a mature effector cell [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040724-40). GO supports the TF interpretation [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0000981).
- **lbx1b** — Supports the obvious hypothesis: ZFIN says it is expressed in nervous system/neural plate/neural tube/spinal cord neural keel and involved in muscle cell differentiation [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050309-27). GO “muscle cell differentiation” is a real process in which unspecialized cells acquire muscle features [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0042692).
- **lbx1a/lbx1b alternative** — A neural-interneuron hypothesis is credible: curated publication summary says zebrafish lbx genes are strongly expressed in hindbrain and spinal cord neural tube [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-111122-7).
- **pitx2** — Pulls away from a pure spinal interneuron call: expressed in brain, dental epithelium, digestive system, head, and mesoderm [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990714-27); curated figure highlights pharyngeal/dental epithelium expression [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-IMAGE-071005-81).
- **hspd1/hspe1** — Heat-shock/chaperonin markers support stress/metabolic load, not identity; GO protein folding fits this module [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0006457), and **hspe1** is broadly expressed including digestive system, midbrain, pectoral fin, segmental plate [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000906-2).

## Caveats
- Competing hypotheses: **lbx-positive neural tube interneuron progenitors** vs **migratory muscle/appendicular muscle precursor**. Both are supported by lbx genes; pitx2 and stress chaperones broaden, not resolve.
- Without canonical motor-neuron, muscle structural, or dental epithelial markers in the provided list, I would not call a mature cell type.

**Verdict:** lbx-positive embryonic neuromuscular developmental population, progenitor — confidence medium

transcript.content: Cluster 52's top up-regulated markers are: en1b, foxd3, slc32a1, pax2a, slc6a5, ube2ql1, stxbp1a, atp6v0cb. Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely: glycinergic inhibitory interneuron, mature — probably hindbrain/spinal rather than neural crest.**

## Evidence
- **slc6a5** — GlyT2; expressed in CNS/glycinergic neurons, with records for spinal cord glycinergic/inhibitory interneurons and hindbrain; GO supports glycinergic synaptic transmission and glycine import. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050105-2) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050105-2?utm_source=openai))
- **slc32a1** — vesicular inhibitory amino-acid transporter; expressed in brain, spinal cord, and inhibitory interneuron; GO supports GABA/glycine transport and neurotransmitter loading into synaptic vesicle. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-061201-1) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-061201-1?utm_source=openai))
- **pax2a** — nervous-system developmental TF; ZFIN/ZFA links pax2a expression to spinal cord interneuron and hindbrain interneuron anatomy, supporting an interneuron identity. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-8) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-8?utm_source=openai))
- **en1b** — expressed in nervous system/neural tube and midbrain–hindbrain boundary; GO/ZFIN description includes neuron fate commitment, consistent with a CNS neuronal/interneuron program. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-6) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-6?utm_source=openai))
- **foxd3** — strongly associated with neural crest, but the simultaneous **slc6a5/slc32a1** inhibitory-neuron program argues against calling this neural crest alone. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-143) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-143?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- Region is ambiguous: markers support CNS glycinergic inhibitory interneuron, but not cleanly hindbrain vs spinal cord.
- **foxd3** may indicate developmental admixture or transient progenitor history.

**Verdict:** glycinergic inhibitory interneuron, mature — confidence medium

- **slc6a5** — strong inhibitory/glycinergic evidence: expressed in glycinergic neurons and spinal cord inhibitory interneurons; GO supports glycine transporter activity/synaptic glycinergic function. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050105-2), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0015187)
- **slc32a1** — vesicular inhibitory transporter: expressed in brain, spinal cord, and inhibitory interneuron; GO term “neurotransmitter loading into synaptic vesicle” fits inhibitory neurotransmitter vesicle loading. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-061201-1), [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0098700)
- **pax2a + en1b + slc6a5** — ZFIN expression summaries place all three in spinal cord/spinal cord interneuron contexts, supporting a Pax2/Engrailed inhibitory interneuron identity rather than a generic neuron. [record](https://zfin.org/action/expression/fish-expression-figure-summary?fishID=ZDB-FISH-150901-26986&imagesOnly=false)
- **ZFA spinal cord interneuron** — defined as “a CNS interneuron located in the spinal cord,” and lists pax2a and slc6a5 among genes with many expression figures. [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0000778)
- **foxd3** — alternative hypothesis: neural crest/progenitor. ZFIN places foxd3 in neural crest/neural plate/neural keel, and ZFA neural crest cells are multipotent ectodermal cells. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-143), [record](https://www.zfin.org/action/ontology/term/ZFA%3A0009165)
- **stxbp1a** — broad neuronal/synaptic support, expressed in nervous system and involved in vesicle docking/exocytosis; not cell-type-specific. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050626-106)

## Caveats
- **foxd3** prevents a pure mature interneuron call; it could reflect neural-plate-border/neural-crest contamination or an immature neural state.
- Deepest defensible tier: **CNS spinal inhibitory interneuron**, not a named subtype beyond likely glycinergic/GABAergic.

**Verdict:** spinal cord inhibitory interneuron, mature/neuronal — confidence medium

transcript.content: Cluster 53's top up-regulated markers are: clu, ntn1b, spon1b, slit1b, sparc, shha, slit2, shhb. Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely identity: floor plate cell / ventral neural-tube midline secretory glial cell.**

## Evidence
- **shha** — strongest match: floor plate anatomy page lists **shha** as the most frequently curated floor-plate-expressed gene; floor plate is defined as ventral-most neural tube and a specialized secretory glial structure. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-21) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-21?utm_source=openai))
- **shhb** — also curated among top floor-plate expression genes, supporting Hedgehog-producing ventral midline identity. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-21) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-21?utm_source=openai))
- **ntn1b** — curated expression includes floor plate / floor plate neural tube; gene is involved in neuron projection development and axon extension regulation. [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-990415-168/expression) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-990415-168/expression?utm_source=openai))
- **spon1b** — curated as repeatedly expressed in floor plate; publication record notes high embryonic floor-plate expression and ECM/neuronal outgrowth relevance. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-200109-2) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-200109-2?utm_source=openai))
- **slit2** — ZFIN image record states **slit2** mRNA is expressed in floor plate cells; GO supports an axon-guidance program. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-IMAGE-090520-7) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-IMAGE-090520-7?utm_source=openai))
- **slit1b / slit2 / ntn1b** — secreted guidance-cue markers align with **axon guidance** biology. [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0007411) ([amigo.geneontology.org](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0007411?utm_source=openai))
- **shha / shhb** — Hedgehog pathway signal fits ventral neural-tube patterning. [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0060831) ([amigo.geneontology.org](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0060831?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- **clu** and **sparc** are less specific; they support secreted/ECM biology but not floor plate alone.

**Verdict:** floor plate cell — confidence high

## Evidence
- **shha** — strongest “obvious” hypothesis: ZFIN curates expression in CNS and mesoderm, and SHH implicates Smoothened/Hedgehog signaling; this fits ventral neural tube/floor-plate or axial midline signaling, not generic neurons. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-166?utm_source=openai))
- **shhb** — reinforces a Hedgehog-producing axial/ventral signaling identity, but ZFIN’s broad gene record alone does not distinguish floor plate from other midline sources. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-980526-41?utm_source=openai))
- **ntn1b** — ZFIN curates expression in CNS, forebrain neural rod, neural plate, head, and hypochord; GO-compatible function is axon guidance/neuron projection development, supporting a midline guidance-cue source. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-168?utm_source=openai))
- **slit2** — expressed in axial mesoderm, forebrain neural tube, hypochord, and nervous system; figure curation specifically notes axial mesoderm, floor plate cells, hypochord, and somites, favoring ventral midline over mature neuronal identity. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-010306-3?utm_source=openai))
- **slit1b** — CNS/forebrain/hindbrain/retinal inner nuclear layer expression supports neural tissue, but not by itself floor plate. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030722-4?utm_source=openai))
- **spon1b / sparc / clu** — extracellular-region/matrix-associated markers add a secreted-ECM/guidance flavor; sparc also raises cartilage/otic/erythroid alternatives, but those are weaker without the Hedgehog + Slit/Netrin midline suite. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000427-10?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- **Alternative 1:** notochord/hypochord/axial mesoderm is plausible because **slit2**, **ntn1b**, and **clu** include axial/hypochord/notochord expression.
- **Alternative 2:** immature CNS guidance-cue cells are plausible, but deepest defensible tier is **ventral midline/axial signaling tissue**, not a named mature neuron/glia subtype.

**Verdict:** ventral midline axial-signaling cells, mature — confidence medium

transcript.content: Cluster 54's top up-regulated markers are: phox2bb, hoxb5b, slit3, phox2a, tenm3, onecut1, nrp1a, gap43. Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely: enteric nervous system neuron / differentiating enteric neuron, mature-leaning but not fully subtype-resolved.**

## Evidence
- **phox2bb** — strongest anchor: expressed in presumptive enteric nervous system/digestive and nervous systems; acts in enteric nervous system development and axonogenesis; knockdown reduces enteric nervous system neurons [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050407-3), [phenotype](https://zfin.org/ZDB-MRPHLNO-050601-1), [GO](https://zfin.org/GO%3A0048484), [anatomy](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0001155).
- **phox2a** — autonomic/catecholaminergic neuronal TF; expressed in nervous system and acts in noradrenergic neuron/locus coeruleus development, supporting neural identity but not ENS specificity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000223-14).
- **hoxb5b** — expressed in nervous system; ZFIN expression includes mid-intestine enteric neuron, fitting posterior/vagal-ENS patterning [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000823-6), [expression](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000823-6/expression).
- **gap43** — neuronal growth/axon marker; expressed in nervous system/neural tube/trigeminal placode and acts in axon regeneration/tissue regeneration, supporting differentiating or neurite-extending neurons [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990415-87).
- **slit3 / nrp1a / tenm3** — axon guidance, neuron projection, synaptic/adhesion programs; support neuronal migration/projection state rather than a non-neural fate [slit3](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-010306-4), [nrp1a](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030519-2), [tenm3](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990714-19).

## Caveats
- No canonical cholinergic/serotonergic/nitrergic ENS subtype marker is provided, so subtype should be left unspecified.
- **phox2bb + hoxb5b** could also mark ENS precursors; **gap43** favors neuronal differentiation/projection growth.

**Verdict:** enteric nervous system neuron, mature — confidence medium
