**Cluster 85 is most defensibly a cerebrospinal-fluid-contacting neuron — likely mature GABAergic sensory CSF-cN.**

## Evidence
- **urp1** — ZFIN anatomy lists **urp1** among the genes most associated with “cerebrospinal fluid contacting neuron”; ZFIN-curated literature reports URP1/URP2 colocalization in spinal CSF-cNs [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0007120).  
- **urp2** — ZFIN describes **urp2** as a urotensin II-related peptide expressed in nervous system/trunk; curated publication summary says Urp1/Urp2 are produced by sensory spinal CSF-cNs [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-110718-3).  
- **pkd2l1** — ZFIN gene record: expressed in spinal cord/spinal cord neural tube; predicted cation-channel activity and acts in mechanosensory behavior, matching CSF-cN sensory identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030616-558).  
- **pkd2l1 / anatomy** — the ZFA term defines CSF-cNs as spinal cord interneurons along the central canal that express PKD2L1 and are chemo-/mechanosensory [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0007120).  
- **slc32a1** — NCBI/GO annotations identify vesicular inhibitory amino-acid transporter activity, GABA transport, and inhibitory synapse localization, supporting GABAergic neuron state [record](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gene/798575).  
- **pkd1l2a / pkd2l1 axis** — GO term “mechanosensitive monoatomic cation channel activity” supports a mechanosensory channel program consistent with PKD-family CSF-cN function [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0140135?relation=isa_partof).  

## Caveats
- **nppc, tal2, si:ch1073-70f20.1** were not needed for the call; I would not treat them as decisive without cluster-specific validation.
- No cycling/progenitor markers are present, so “mature” is inferred from neurotransmitter/neuropeptide/channel markers.

**Verdict:** cerebrospinal-fluid-contacting neuron, mature — confidence high

**Most likely: CNS astroglial / radial glial cell, mature or quiescent glial state — not enough evidence for cycling/progenitor.**

## Evidence
- **gfap** — glial intermediate-filament gene; expressed in nervous system, neural tube, neuronal stem cell; ZFIN astrocyte term lists gfap among top expression-linked genes [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-990914-3), [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009075).
- **slc1a2b** — zebrafish ortholog of glutamate transporter SLC1A2; ZFIN astrocyte term includes slc1a2b expression/antibody labeling, supporting astroglial glutamate uptake identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-7779), [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009075).
- **atp1a1b** — Na⁺/K⁺ ATPase alpha subunit expressed in central nervous system/neural tube; compatible with ion-homeostatic glia but not cell-type-specific alone [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-001212-5).
- **col4a5** — basement-membrane/ECM collagen expressed in nervous system and neural tube; supports glial endfoot/lamina-associated context rather than neuronal identity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-030131-2281).
- **gfap / GO** — GFAP is tied to type III intermediate filament biology, a canonical astroglial structural feature [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0045098).
- **slc1a2b / GO** — implicated function is L-glutamate transmembrane transporter activity, matching astroglial neurotransmitter clearance [record](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO%3A0005313).
- **ZFA anatomy** — astrocyte is a CNS macroglial cell regulating extracellular ionic/chemical environment; radial glial cell remains a plausible zebrafish-specific astroglial morphology [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009075), [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-100331-2349).

## Caveats
- **cldn7a, cav1, col4a5** add epithelial/ECM/barrier flavor, so this may be specialized ependymoglial/barrier-associated astroglia.
- No proliferation markers were provided; “progenitor” is not supported.

**Verdict:** astroglial / radial glial cell, mature/quiescent — confidence medium

[record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-180403-2049) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-TERM-180403-2049?utm_source=openai))

transcript.content: Cluster 89's top up-regulated markers are: rlbp1a, fabp7a, acbd7, cotl1, crabp1a, ckbb, cldn5b, efhd1. Using ZFIN curated expression, ZFA anatomy, and GO, identify the most likely zebrafish cell type (with state if the markers support it), grounding each claim in a cited record. If the evidence is ambiguous, say so.

**Most likely: retinal Müller glia / Müller cell, mature or quiescent-like.**

## Evidence
- **rlbp1a** — visual-system/retina-linked retinoid carrier; ZFIN notes expression in visual system and photoreceptor maintenance, while Schlegel et al. report zebrafish paralog cell-specificity involving retina glia/RPE context [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-1662), [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-211022-43).
- **fabp7a** — fatty-acid binding gene expressed in immature eye and nervous system; also reported with glial/radial-glial contexts, supporting a glial identity rather than retinal neuron [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000627-1), [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-IMAGE-150319-9).
- **crabp1a** — retinoic-acid/fatty-acid binding gene expressed in eye and CNS, consistent with retinal glial retinoid/lipid handling [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-020320-3).
- **acbd7** — predicted fatty-acyl-CoA binding and fatty-acid metabolic process; expressed in CNS, adding lipid-metabolic support but not cell-type specificity [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-050913-108), [record](https://zfin.org/action/marker/ZDB-GENE-050913-108/expression).
- **Muller cell** — ZFA defines this as a retinal glial cell spanning retinal thickness, with bodies in the inner nuclear layer [record](https://zfin.org/ZFA%3A0009280).
- **cldn5b** — vascular/tight-junction marker expressed in cardiovascular/brain structures and cranial vasculature; this is discordant with a pure Müller-glia call and may reflect barrier/endothelial admixture [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041010-140), [record](https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-FIG-220801-227).

## Caveats
- **rlbp1a** can mark retinal pigment epithelium contexts, while Müller glia more classically use the paralog **rlbp1b**; **rlbp1b is not in this cluster’s marker list**.
- No cycling markers are provided, so “progenitor/activated” is not supported.

**Verdict:** Muller cell / retinal Müller glia, mature/quiescent-like — confidence medium

**Most defensible call: visual-system glial/RPE-like cell, not deeper than retina-associated support cell; Müller glia vs retinal pigment epithelium remains ambiguous.**

## Evidence
- **rlbp1a** — strongest visual-cycle marker: curated as expressed in visual system/optic vesicle/brain, with rlbp1a loss affecting retinal pigment epithelium, Müller-cell labeling, photoreceptor maintenance and optokinetic behavior [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-1662). Schlegel reports rlbp1a paralog expression in RPE, while another ZFIN-indexed record reports rlbp1a in Müller glia, so it supports retinal support identity but not a single cell type. ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-040426-1662?utm_source=openai))
- **fabp7a** — supports glial/neuroepithelial alternative: expressed in nervous system, immature eye and neural tube; ZFIN figure notes Fabp7a colocalization in cerebellar Bergmann glia, and literature summary links fabp7a to radial glial progenitor differentiation/perineurial glia. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000627-1) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-000627-1?utm_source=openai))
- **crabp1a** — retinoic-acid/retinoid-binding program is compatible with eye/retinal support cells, but its ZFIN expression evidence is tissue-subfunctionalized rather than cell-type decisive. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-050714-8) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-PUB-050714-8?utm_source=openai))
- **cldn5b** — alternative endothelial hypothesis: cldn5b is expressed in cardiovascular system/brain and curated with tight-junction assembly/cell adhesion; ZFIN figures identify arterial/cranial vascular endothelial expression, arguing possible endothelial contamination or vascular-associated cells. [record](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041010-140) ([zfin.org](https://zfin.org/ZDB-GENE-041010-140?utm_source=openai))
- ZFA/GO grounding: OLS provides the zebrafish anatomy framework for retina/visual-system terming, and GO defines the functional vocabulary; here, marker GO points to lipid/retinoid binding and tight junctions rather than one exclusive cell type. ([ebi.ac.uk](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/materials/bioinformatics-functional-genomics-zebrafish-materials/resources-for-analysing-zebrafish-data/zebrafish-anatomy/?utm_source=openai))

## Caveats
- No canonical Müller marker or RPE pigmentation marker is in the provided list.
- Deepest defensible tier: **visual-system/retina-associated support cell**, not definitive Müller glia or RPE.

**Verdict:** retina-associated support cell, mature — confidence medium**
